string.text: Settings of other mods in one place. Links are defined in configs\rezone\rezone_mcm_links.ltx and only show for installed mods.
No links yet (or the target mods are not installed).
Jumps to that mod's MCM page.
Changes the original mod's setting directly.
Off = ReZone does not touch hits at all. Vanilla damage or another mod applies.
By attacking mutant (stacks with hit type)
Multiplies all hit types (presets don't change it).
How much mutants can take. 2.0 = twice as much. Applies instantly.
Prints what ReZone MCM does. Testing only.

Traders neither buy nor sell weapons, outfits and helmets. You get gear from corpses, friends and stashes, repair it and strip it for parts. Nothing is deleted, it is just hidden in the trade window or can't be sold - turning it off brings everything back.
Main switch. Off = trading as before.
Traders don't buy any of it
Weapons (and outfits with helmets) from your inventory can't be sold - the trader isn't interested.
Traders don't sell any of it
Weapons (and outfits with helmets) disappear from traders' stock.
Off = knives can still be bought and sold. Grenades, ammo and attachments are never restricted.
Weapons = pistols, SMGs, rifles, shotguns and sniper rifles. Grenades, ammo, attachments and parts are never restricted.
Traders do not buy weapons (ReZone: GAMMA-style trading)
Price multiplier by item kind. 1.0 = unchanged, 2.0 = double. Applies to buying and selling, overall multipliers separately.
Warning: Configurable Item Cost Modifiers is also enabled. Disable it, otherwise prices are multiplied twice.
Off = prices as without the mod (or by another mod).
Sets the sliders below. You can tweak them afterwards.
What the trader pays you. 0.6 = 60 % of the price.
What you pay the trader. 1.2 = 20 % more.
Condition of weapons, outfits and helmets dropped by dead NPCs and how much ammo they carry. Set a range for novices and for legends, ranks in between are interpolated.
Sets the sliders below, tweak them afterwards.
Multiplier of ammo found on bodies. 1.0 = vanilla.
"_bad" ammo becomes regular. With Arti ballistics / ReZone Ballistics "_bad" are special rounds (7N22, incendiary, HP...), so this removes them from loot.

How many stalkers and mutants live in the Zone, how fast they come back and how big squads and packs are. ReZone's own system, no other mod needed. Only common squads from respawn and game start are changed; story characters and task spawns stay untouched.
Off = vanilla Anomaly (density from Options > ALife applies).
Sets all sliders at once, you can fine-tune them afterwards.
Density and squad size apply to newly spawned squads. On a new game they apply to the whole Zone right away.
How many stalker squads appear at smart terrains (1 = vanilla, 0 = none). Replaces the setting in Options > ALife.
How many mutant packs appear (1 = vanilla, 0 = none). Replaces the setting in Options > ALife.
Multiplier of the time before a smart terrain respawns (1 = vanilla, usually 12 game hours; 2 = twice as long, 0.5 = twice as fast).
Multiplier of people per squad (1 = vanilla). New members copy existing ones, the leader stays.
Random spread of size (0 = always the same, 0.5 = from half to one and a half).
When stalkers respawn, sometimes one more squad that normally appears on this level shows up. Not at faction bases.
Multiplier of mutants per pack (1 = vanilla).
Random spread of pack size (0 = always the same).
When mutants respawn, sometimes one more pack that normally lives on this level shows up.
No strong stalkers on starting levels

Generic stalkers of all factions above the chosen rank (veterans and masters in heavy suits and exoskeletons) don't spawn on the selected levels - a weaker version of the same faction replaces them - and strong squads from other levels don't travel there. Those already there leave over time. Story characters, traders and mutants unchanged. Works even without ReZone population enabled.
Up to which class generic stalkers may be on the selected levels.
Faction bases (e.g. Clear Sky in the Swamps) keep their strong members.
You cannot sell helmets to them. Works even without GAMMA trading.
Helmets disappear from their offer (not deleted, back when turned off).
Trader stock limits: after every restock the trader keeps only a limited number of items from each group, the rest disappears. -1 = no limit.
Applies at the next restock (vanilla every 24 h). Does not touch companions, what the trader wears, or quest items.
Items are counted per piece (ammo boxes, packs). Items you sold are not limited until the next restock.
Own damage calculation for NPCs and mutants hit by your bullets. Ammo data: configs\rezone\ammo.ltx. NPC vs NPC fights are calculated by the game as before.

How your shots on NPCs are calculated and also the profile of the suits you wear. CoP = Call of Pripyat, Anomaly = slightly softer NPCs, Hardcore = lethal headshots and armor breaking. The suit profile applies after loading a save.
CoP: if the round beats the armor, damage drops by (AP - armor) / AP; if not, only blunt impact gets through. Use AP rounds against armored targets, regular ones against unarmored.
Extra multiplier on top of the preset (2 = NPCs take twice as much).
Casings, powder and bullets on bodies, in stashes and at traders (0 = none, 1 = default).
How many boxes one craft of regular ammo gives (special ammo always 1).

How much condition a suit or helmet loses when hit (1 = vanilla, 0.33 = three times slower, 0 = none). Replaces the armor_degradation_reduction DLTX - delete it, otherwise it multiplies. Applies after loading a save.

Helmets (ReZone's own separated helmets): every suit has a helmet slot and only the helmet protects the head. Closed suits (SEVA, exo, Nosorog, NBC, SSP) lost their built-in mask - part of their radiation, psy and chemical protection is now in the helmet. Helmet armor follows the suit profile above. The Separated Helmets mod is no longer needed.

Off = like vanilla: closed suits (SEVA, exo, Nosorog...) have no helmet slot again, full mask protection and the head protected by the suit itself. Helmets for other suits stay. Applies after loading a save.
A dead stalker in a closed suit (SEVA, exo, ...) also drops the matching helmet when his model has no separate one. Same drop rules as the suit. List: configs\rezone\helmets.ltx.
How much damage you take, per hit type. 1 = no change (vanilla).
Sets all hit types at once, fine-tune afterwards.

All damage you take is set only here. Call of Pripyat (beginners): bullets x0.35, mutants x0.4, falls and blows x0.5, explosions x0.3, fire x0.65, anomalies, radiation and psi x0.75. Anomaly: bullets x0.7. Hardcore: everything stronger. Everything at 1 = vanilla.
Recipes in the vanilla workshop and extra tabs (Hideout, Backpacks, Magazines). What happens to recipes after reading.
The read recipe is removed from the inventory. Known recipes are in the PDA (Encyclopedia > Notes).
When you read a recipe you already know, it stays in the inventory so you can sell it.
Video behind the main menu and the load screen. Put .ogm (Theora) videos into gamedata\textures\ui\rz_mm_bg\ - each one shows up here by its name.
Default = background from your UI mods unchanged. Random = a different video on every start (and when changed).
Applies right after Apply. New videos in the folder show up in the list after restarting the game. File names in lower case without spaces (e.g. zaton_night.ogm).

One choice sets all of ReZone for a play style - ballistics, armor and wear, player damage, mutant toughness, loot, prices, traders and their stock, artefacts and population - and with EFT Health System its difficulty too. Wandering stalkers and trade bans (Play like GAMMA, helmets) are never turned on by a preset, you enable them yourself.
Custom = nothing changes, your settings on the individual pages apply.

Call of Pripyat: bullets on the player x0.35, anomalies and radiation x0.75, CoP armor, slow wear, weaker mutants and explosions, artefacts and mutant parts sell well, traders sell everything, usable gear from bodies, calmer Zone, learned recipes are kept, EFTH difficulty Call of Pripyat.
Anomaly: bullets x0.7, Anomaly armor, prices and trade like vanilla Anomaly, vanilla mutants, usable gear from bodies, vanilla population, EFTH difficulty Normal.

Hardcore: bullets x1.5 and everything stronger, lethal headshots, armor breaking, full wear, tougher mutants, GAMMA-like economy (gear sells cheap, limited stock), little usable loot, dangerous Zone, EFTH difficulty Hardcore.

All options the preset changes are marked right after you pick it (change count at the bottom) and saved on Apply. Afterwards you can fine-tune anything by hand - the preset won't overwrite it until you change it again. Prices, trade and effects are not changed. Population applies to newly spawned squads.
Turns off the screen distortion (PPE) that appears when you are near a monster or radiation. Sounds, damage, psy attacks and monster behaviour stay the same - only the on-screen effect is gone.
Radiation fields and the radiation aura of monsters (e.g. poltergeist, controller, mutants from radioactive spots).
Psy aura and the 'scanning' effect when the poltergeist is detecting you.
The controller's psy aura (distortion near him). The 'tunnel' attack stays.
Chance of ammo with a weapon
How often a corpse also has ammo for its weapon (1 = always as in vanilla, 0.5 = half of corpses). The amount is set by the slider above.
Items on corpses - chance (how often) and count (how many). 1 = vanilla, 0 = never, 2 = double. Categories by item kind; guaranteed items (story characters' items) are not changed.
Medkits, bandages, antirad, stimulants, splints and other meds.
How many at once when they drop.
How many at once when they drop.
How many at once when they drop.
Tools, parts, batteries, documents, trinkets and everything else.
How many at once when they drop.
Minimum condition of items to sell (%)

Minimum condition at which traders buy weapons and gear. Replaces Anomaly's Gameplay > Economy > minimum item condition, which resets to 0 in every save - ReZone sets it to this value after loading. 0 = keep the save's value.
Anomaly won't let you use a med or drug while an earlier one with a stronger effect is still active (the 'stronger effect' message). This turns it off without editing itms_manager.script.
Meds, stimulants and drugs can be used any time, even while another is active.
Other conditions stay: missing tool, anabiotic in combat, EFTH 'nothing to treat'. Applies right away.

How much bushes, tree crowns and other see-through obstacles hide the player from NPCs. In vanilla stalkers see through bushes almost as if they weren't there. 0 = vanilla, 0.5 = a denser bush hides you, 1 = anything see-through (even glass) hides you completely. Walls and terrain always block.
When the stalker doesn't know about you (patrol, camp). This matters most for sneaking.
When the stalker is alerted or fighting. Higher = easier to lose him in the bushes.
All mutants, including modded ones (Re:Spawn etc.).

Grass and reeds are not affected - they have no collision in the game, so NPC sight always passes through. Applies to NPCs loaded after the change - most reliably after loading a save. Requires modded exes. Game files are not changed.
Hits on the player: the blood direction marker showing where a bullet came from, and the camera kick (aim punch) when you are hit.
The blood marker showing the hit direction disappears. Hit sound, damage and blood effects stay.
Disable camera kick on hit (aim punch)
Camera and weapon no longer jerk when you are hit - turns off both the engine kick and Anomaly's camera animations on bigger wounds. The red flash and pain sound stay.
Camera kick applies right away. The marker disappears after loading a save or changing level (with both turned off it disappears right away). Requires modded exes.
Applies to monsters and radiation fields loaded after the change - most reliably after loading a save. Requires modded exes. Game files are not changed.

Small stalker squads walk across the level from place to place and stay a while at each, so the Zone feels alive outside camps too. They appear only far from you, never at faction bases and never in labs or underground. At night, after a while or when the level is switched off they disappear again - only when far away or out of sight. Levels and factions are listed in configs\rezone\wander.ltx.
Off = nothing spawns; squads already walking disappear over time.
How many wandering squads may be on one level at once.
Average time between new squads (randomly half to one and a half).
After this time the squad disappears as soon as it is far from you.
A squad never appears or disappears closer than this.
At night no new squads appear and those outside fade away.
When you travel to another level the wandering squads are removed (companions stay).
Only factions living on the level
The squad is only from a faction that has a place on the level. Off = any enabled faction.

How often artefacts grow in anomaly fields and how strong they are. Each field has its own groups by location: mostly junk and weak ones in Cordon, medium further in the Zone, strong ones in Pripyat, the labs and near the plant. Strength follows ReZone's Call of Pripyat style artefacts (weak, medium, strong). New artefacts grow after an emission or a psi storm.
Off = vanilla Anomaly group choice and chance. The field and strength groups apply always.
Sets the sliders at once, you can fine-tune them afterwards.
Multiplier of the chance that an artefact grows when a field renews (1 = by economy difficulty, 0 = never, 2 = twice as often).
Chance multiplier after a psi storm (vanilla 0.7).
How often a field picks a weaker or stronger group it offers.
Call of Pripyat - strong ones rare
Chances apply to fields that renew after the change (after the next emission or psi storm).
How much damage a mutant attack deals to you, by species. 0.5 = half, 2.0 = double. Multiplies with Player damage (Mutants).
Off = mutant attacks follow Player damage only.
ReSpawn Mutants - new mutants from the mod
How fast hunger, thirst and sleepiness grow. 1 = vanilla Anomaly, 0.5 = twice as slow, 2 = twice as fast, 0 = doesn't grow at all. Food, drinks, sleep and energy drinks work the same as before.
How fast satiety drops (energy with EFTH).
How fast thirst grows, also while sleeping (hydration with EFTH).
How fast the need to sleep grows. How much sleep removes stays the same.
Applies right away. Thirst and sleepiness only work when enabled in Options > Gameplay. Game files are not changed.

How much a stalker can take depending on his rank. 1 = vanilla, 2 = takes twice as much, 0.5 = half. Applies to all damage (player, NPCs, mutants, anomalies, grenades) and right away to NPCs already in the game. Armor and headshots work the same - the value is an extra multiplier.
Result = rank x All stalkers. Scripted kills from other mods (silent kills, story) are not changed. Game files are not changed.
Binoculars (and scopes with the 'auto target capture' upgrade) frame stalkers and mutants and mark enemies. You can turn it off here - then you have to spot targets with your own eyes.
On = vanilla. Off = binoculars only zoom.
Applies after loading a save (or to newly acquired binoculars). Also works for binoculars and scopes from mods. Requires modded exes. Game files are not changed.
How much a novice can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a trainee can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a experienced stalker can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a professional can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a veteran can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a expert can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a master can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
How much a legend can take. 1 = vanilla, 2 = twice as many hits, 0.5 = half. He only gets (damage / this value). The total is also multiplied by All stalkers.
Multiplies all ranks at once. E.g. All 2 and Veteran 1.5 = a veteran takes 3x more than in vanilla.

All PDAs (1, 2, 3 and PDAs from mods) show characters in range on the minimap - PDA 1 about 68 m, PDA 2 120 m, PDA 3 240 m. When someone dies, a grey dot stays. Here you can hide corpses on the minimap, so you have to find them yourself.
On = vanilla (grey dots of the dead). Off = corpses are not shown on the minimap with any PDA. Living characters stay.
Hiding corpses applies after loading a save or changing level. Persistent dots apply right away. Game files are not changed.
Zone Customization Project is installed. Both population settings would stack - use only one of them.
On = like GAMMA, outfits and helmets can't be bought or sold either. Off = weapons only.

Vanilla closes the window after every action. On = workshop (craft, repair, upgrade), cooking and repair kits stay open with the same selection. The window closes when the cooker or repair kit runs out.
Every character and mutant that dies near you gets a minimap dot regardless of PDA range. The dot disappears once you search the body. Only works with corpses on minimap enabled.

How much disassembled ammo gives back - a share of exactly the items it is crafted from in the workshop (0.5 = half). E.g. Dragon's Breath returns buckshot shells plus fire and star powder, not generic parts. Ammo without a recipe is disassembled the old way.

NPCs with a knife sometimes rush the player, a stalker or a mutant in combat and stab them - ambush, close attack, mutant hunting and defence against mutants. Port of rx_knife from AI Additions (Rulix aka Bak). More settings in configs\misc\rz_npc_knife.ltx.
Off = NPCs do not attack with knives and get no knives (like vanilla).
Chance an NPC without a knife gets one (0 = never, 0.35 = default). Each NPC is rolled only once.
Multiplier of NPC courage. Higher = they charge with a knife more often and from further away (1 = default, factions have their own courage in the LTX).
Multiplier of the extra damage when an NPC stabs you (on top of the knife's own damage; 1 = default, 0 = knife only).
NPCs go after weaker mutants with knives on their own. Close defence against mutants always works.
Traders, quest givers and other story characters do not attack with knives.
An NPC shouts at the start of a knife attack (one of two sounds at random).
Changes apply immediately. Knife chance and story characters apply to NPCs loaded after the change. A specific NPC can be excluded in its logic: can_use_knife = false.
